name: message
description: One turn of a task and answer exchange: a filled prompt panel or an outlined, right-aligned answer, with an optional label, an optional note line and optional inline corrections.

props.name: variant
props.description: prompt (filled bg-surface-pressed panel), answer (outlined, right-aligned) or task (inverted: text-active fill, bg-surface text, the text in title type (body size, bold)). Other values fall back to prompt.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional small uppercase caption above the text.

props.name: segments
props.description: Optional list of {text, kind?, tooltip?, href?, current?} replacing `text`. A segment with kind remove or add renders as an inline-mark (with its tooltip); others are plain text.

props.name: note
props.description: Optional plain text under the text, in text-subactive (e.g. the instruction that goes with a question).

props.name: note_tooltip
props.description: Optional tooltip text (newlines start new lines) shown by a "(more)" trigger at the end of the note: dotted underline, focusable. The note's own text stays plain.

props.name: note_more
props.description: Label of the note's tooltip trigger (in brackets after the note).

props.name: tail
props.description: Draft (2026-10-29). start | end: a small triangle at the bottom corner on that side, in the message's fill (outlined for the answer variant), so the box reads as a chat message. The box keeps spacing-4 of room on that side.

props.name: note_tone
props.description: Draft (2026-10-29). success: the note in the success color (inline-mark's add color), set apart from the text above by a hairline divider, for the corrected version of that text.

props.name: inverted
props.description: Draft (2026-10-29). The task's inverted fill (text-active fill, surface-colored text) for a prompt or an answer, keeping the body type; a success note switches to the untinted success green, readable on both themes' inverted fill.

rationale: A task and the learner's reply are two voices, so they differ by shape, not only by color: the prompt is a filled panel (bg-surface-pressed), the answer is outlined with the hairline token and aligned to the right. Padding is spacing-5 for both; the text uses the body type, the label the data role in uppercase and text-subactive, so the label reads as a caption. Segments let the same box show a corrected sentence by composing inline-mark; the plain-text path covers every other case. Arrangement of messages in a column (gaps, a pinned input) is the host's layout, not part of this component. No Figma node: taken from the application's design canvas of 2026-10-21. The optional note is a second line under the text in the body type and text-subactive: a question and the instruction that goes with it are one turn, and the color alone ranks them without a new type style. The task variant opens a turn: inversion and the title type (the body size, bold) make the question the first thing read, ahead of the answer and the feedback under it, without a new color. 2026-10-29 (draft, explicit request): tail adds the chat-message triangle at a bottom corner (start for the other voice, end for the user's), drawn with clip-path in the message's own fill; the outlined answer draws the outline triangle under the fill one so its border continues into the tail.
a11y_notes: Plain divs of text; no role. A host that shows a conversation should put the messages in a list or a log region and say who speaks (the label can carry it). Corrections come from inline-mark; see its notes on conveying removed and added text to assistive technology.
